title: Generic local finite presentation over an integral base
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $S$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. There exists a nonempty open $U\subseteq S$ such that the restricted morphism $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tags 051T and 052A, finite-presentation clauses; proofs read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/051T and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/052A

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open Spec A of S and a finite affine cover Spec B_i of its inverse image. For each finite type A-algebra B, apply the existing proved torsion-cover theorem from Sheaf.RingTheory.GenericFlatness (imported with import all) to obtain a finitely presented algebra C and a surjection C→B whose kernel is A-torsion. That theorem constructs C by lifting finitely many relation generators over Frac(A) after clearing denominators. Generic flatness applied to Spec C→Spec A gives a nonzero a for which C_a is flat over A_a, hence torsion free. The localized kernel vanishes, so C_a≅B_a. Localization preserves finite presentation, hence B_a is finitely presented over A_a. Intersect the finitely many basic opens, which all contain the generic point. Locality on the source proves local finite presentation of the restricted map. An empty cover gives the whole affine base.
